assumptions: No other code depends on the old discard-to-defaults behavior of loadConfig weight validation (only consumer is context-assembler reading named keys).
±0.01 tolerance from the original check is the settled tolerance for both the rule-1 completeness test and the already-normalized merged check.
context: Fixed #34: loadConfig no longer discards user priority_weights when a partial set deep-merges over 1.0 — user sets summing to ~1.0 are treated as complete (missing keys 0), otherwise merged weights rescale proportionally; defaults only on invalid input.
rationale: after deepMerge, user-provided keys are indistinguishable from defaults, which was the root cause of #34; the alternative of threading an explicitness flag through deepMerge would churn every merge call for one key.
summary: Chose to resolve priority_weights from the raw parsed YAML (parsed.context_assembly.priority_weights) rather than the deep-merged config
